title: Terminal and Echo
premise: Mara Pemberton, a clone of the murdered colony founder, inherits both the dead woman's memories and her unsolved murder case. As the colony's children begin sharing a dream that turns out to be a leaked memory archive, Mara discovers the original's killer is alive inside the fleet's command structure — and that the truce between colony and fleet rests on a lie the original built to keep two armed fleets apart. To expose the killer would shatter the truce; to preserve it, Mara must let the murder stand unsolved while quietly dismantling the killer's power. In the end, Mara chooses truth over vengeance, broadcasting the original's final memory as testimony rather than evidence, and the children's dream becomes the shared inheritance that holds both fleets together instead of tearing them apart.
about_author: Emrys Crane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years coordinating supply runs between research stations before turning to fiction. Their work explores how memory, identity, and obligation survive transmission across distance.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Mara Pemberton pilots the supply run between the colony Vessel and the fleet anchor, narrating in first person as she catalogs the inherited memories that aren't hers. She introduces the truce: the fleet and colony haven't spoken directly in eleven years, only through couriers like her. Emotional beat: loneliness braided with duty, and the first flicker of doubt about who she is beyond the original's echo.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Ivo Reyes reports that nine children woke describing the identical dream: a white room, a woman's voice counting down. Mara recognizes the room from the original's memories — the founder's sealed lab, destroyed before her death. POV shifts to Ivo. Emotional beat: unease curdling into wonder as the colony realizes something buried is surfacing.

chapters.title: Inheritance Audit
chapters.summary: Mara examines the original's legal bequest and finds a sealed addendum she was never granted access to, unlocked by the children's dream phrase. Inside: a partial confession naming a killer by rank, not name — a fleet officer. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the thrill of inheritance turning to horror as she realizes her memories were curated, not complete.

chapters.title: Truce Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Captain Sunde negotiates the annual resupply and probes Mara about the children, revealing the fleet knows more than it should. Mara realizes the dream is leaking through the comm relay both sides share. POV: Sunde. Emotional beat: Sunde's cold professionalism masking fear that the truce — and her own complicity — is unraveling.

chapters.title: What the Original Buried
chapters.summary: Mara descends into the flooded ruins of the founder's lab with Ivo's eldest student, Tali, whose dreams are most vivid. They recover a data core containing the original's final recording. POV: Tali. Emotional beat: Tali's awe at dreaming another woman's death, and the dawning weight of being made a witness.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: The core reveals the original faked her own research results to convince both fleets the colony was strategically worthless — the lie that ended the standoff and got her killed by the officer who wanted it exploited. Mara must decide: reveal the truth and restart the standoff, or bury it and the murder together. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the crushing arithmetic of loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: The fleet's truce review board arrives early; Sunde warns Mara the officer from the confession — now Fleet Director Voss — is coming in person. The children's shared dream intensifies, now including Voss's voice. POV: Sunde. Emotional beat: dread and a flicker of conscience as Sunde chooses, quietly, to help Mara instead of reporting her.

chapters.title: Voss Descending
chapters.summary: Voss arrives, charming and surgical, and privately offers Mara a new identity and full records of her own creation in exchange for the data core. Mara realizes he knows exactly what she is — and that he helped make her. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: temptation, violation, and the cold clarity of understanding her own origin as leverage.

chapters.title: The Dream Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Voss moves to seize the core and silence the children; Mara, Sunde, Ivo, and Tali broadcast the original's final memory — not as evidence of murder, but as testimony of the lie — to both fleets simultaneously, letting every colonist and officer dream it together. Voss is arrested by his own board rather than martyred into a war cause. Emotional beat: terrifying exposure becoming collective witness.

chapters.title: Terminal and Echo
chapters.summary: Resolution. The fleets open direct channels for the first time in eleven years; the original is publicly mourned, her murder formally closed with Voss's conviction. Mara, no longer merely an echo, chooses her own name and stays as the colony's first elected voice. The children still dream, but now the dream belongs to everyone. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance, shared.
